_comment: SPARK — S175 P4a: THE VOLTKIN TV, AS A BUILDING (owner, S175).
Owner: "we're redoing the whole way that Voltkin is coming out of the TV. It's gonna be in game.
It's gonna be like the tower is being built ... kind of like when bosses come out. But even cooler."
And on what he sees today: "for now it's just fucking connectors of, what is it, four squares and
then four triangle. It looks stupid. It should be like that, but then the tower happens."
⭐ THREE ROWS, NOT SIX, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE DE-RISK. His art is a six-panel sequence — intact,
spawn, burning, critical, explosion, ruins — but the engine's TowerState union is
intact/damaged/destroyed, and WIDENING it breaks tsc across BOTH row tables (T3 and T9) and forces
a decision about rows the tier-9 sheets do not have. Mapping his sequence onto the three states the
renderer already drives costs nothing and ships now:
intact    <- tv-1-intact
damaged   <- tv-3-burning   (his own words: the long-lived state the tower wears most of a match)
destroyed <- tv-6-ruins
⚠ tv-2-spawn, tv-4-critical and tv-5-explosion are NOT packed here. They belong to the emergence
and the destruction cinematic, which are frame-driven and client-local (the TOWER_CRUMBLE_FRAMES
shape), not damage states. Packing them into this sheet would put four-of-six rows somewhere no
code reads and invite a future session to 'wire up the missing rows'.
⚠ THE SOURCES ARE FLATTENED ONTO 254-WHITE first (`*-flat.png`). The packer's matte keys out
near-WHITE; a transparent PNG whose RGB is 0,0,0 reads as SUBJECT and packs the art inside a black
box. That cost S175 three rebuilds on the direwolf before it was spotted by LOOKING at the sheet.
⚠ NO normaliseStateScale — buildings legitimately change size between states, and a burning TV that
has partly collapsed SHOULD be shorter than an intact one. `fit: box` and framesPerState 1 match
every other building spec in the tree.

damaged._why: His BURNING panel, not CRITICAL. He called burning the state the tower wears most of the match; critical is one beat before the explosion and belongs to the destruction sequence.
